A skewed asset-liability profile could lead to a liquidity crunch, resulting in significantly higher funding costs. The company has a diversified funding profile in terms of products, institutions, and countries, with a base of 76 lenders comprising a healthy mix of banks, non-banks, and global impact lenders.

The Company employs prudent asset-liquidity management and maintains a well-diversified liability profile to minimize market turbulence impacts. A rating upgrade to A (Stable) may provide easier credit and liquidity terms. We continuously monitor market liquidity conditions.
Negative: Financial loss Positive: Strong Financial Position. Strengthened Impact Parameters. Enabling last mile reach.

Customer experience is a significant opportunity to enhance our competitiveness and build lasting relationships with our clients. By delivering exceptional services and products, we can increase customer satisfaction, retention, and loyalty. Given that the company provides financial products and services to millions of customers, any undesirable customer experience could result in loss of customers or even reputational loss.

To maximize the opportunity of customer experience, we have adopted the following approach: Digital Innovation: Embracing new age, cutting edge technologies and leveraging innovative technologies through our “PhyGital” model which uses technology and authentic in -person service to create loans which support the ambitions of our customers. We engage directly with our clients and work through loan applications together, in person, at the customer’s pace. Grievance Redressal Mechanisms: We have a dedicated grievance redressal mechanism “Sparsh” to promptly address customer related complaints and grievances through multiple channels. Each complaint is thoroughly reviewed, monitored, and resolved to achieve complete customer satisfaction. We monitor customer queries and grievances on various social media channels and provide quick resolution.

Negative: Loss of reputation can result in loss of customers thereby adversely impacting business. Positive: By providing superior customer experience, we can differentiate ourselves from competitors and attract new customers seeking exceptional financial services.

Dependence on technology platforms and associated vendors heightens the system’s vulnerability. In the event of a security breach, sensitive customer information could be exposed, leading to regulatory fines, legal liabilities, loss of customer trust, and damage to the company’s brand image.Ensuring robust data protection measures is essential to safeguard the interests of both - the institution and its client.

We have enhanced our IT infrastructure and Information Security team to effectively monitor and address these challenges on an ongoing basis. We have a well- defined framework and policy on cyber security and data privacy. This policy assures users that all personal information provided through the website is treated with the utmost confidentiality and is not shared with third parties in most circumstances, unless explicitly solicited and permitted by the user.

Financial implications of the risk or opportunity (indicate positive or negative implications)

Financing has an important role to play in enabling businesses and economies to transition to a sustainable economy. The NBFC-MFI sector in India is one of the key drivers of the economy and significantly contributes to the country’s GDP as well as employment. As a financial services company, we recognize that directing capital towards such small businesses presents a substantial opportunity for us to make a meaningful impact. We firmly believe that achieving financial success should be intricately linked with our contribution to the greater good of society

Being an NBFC-MFI, focusing on providing loans to income generating businesses in the rural and semi-urban areas that are underserved, we are addressing a major financing gap, thus, enabling such businesses and entrepreneurs to obtain loans to scale up their operations, improve efficiency and for other business expansion related purposes. Our efforts involve placing a heightened focus on providing loans to women entrepreneurs with a focus on sustainability and inclusive growth.
Positive: Attracting impact investors, improving reputation and promoting sustainability in lending helps in identifying risk and opportunities.

Under penetration and untapped market presents a huge opportunity for growth for NBFC-MFIs. Millions of individuals, especially in rural and semi-urban areas, remain excluded from the formal credit system. This credit gap results from a lack of access to traditional banking services, limited credit history, and various other socio-economic factors, etc. With increasing focus of the government towards financial inclusion, rising financial awareness, and increasing smartphone and internet penetration, there is a significant potential for expanding the reach of NBFC-MFIs.

We have a presence in 26 states and union territories. To adapt to and mitigate risks while tapping into underpenetrated markets, we implement comprehensive risk management strategies. These strategies include developing robust credit scoring models using alternative data sources, leveraging advanced technologies for predictive analytics and fraud detection, and diversifying our portfolio across regions and sectors. Establishing strong governance and compliance practices, along with regular audits, ensures operational stability and adherence to regulations. We invest in staff training and educate our clients on responsible borrowing to further reduce default risks.

Positive: More Market expansion. Demonstrating a commitment to financial inclusion aligns with evolving consumer preferences and enhances our reputation as a socially responsible financial institution.

We firmly believe that achieving financial success should be intricately linked with our contribution to the greater good of society.

Being an NBFC-MFI, focusing on providing loans to income generating businesses in the rural and semi-urban areas that are underserved, we are addressing a major financing gap, thus, enabling such businesses and entrepreneurs to obtain loans to scale up their operations, improve efficiency and for other business expansion related purposes. Our efforts involve placing a heightened focus on providing loans to women entrepreneurs with a focus on sustainability and inclusive growth.
Attracting impact investors, improving reputation and promoting sustainability in lending helps in identifying risk and opportunities.

Under penetration and untapped market presents a huge opportunity for growth for NBFC-MFIs. Millions of individuals, especially in rural and semi-urban areas, remain excluded from the formal credit system. This credit gap results from a lack of access to traditional banking services, limited credit history, and various other socio-economic factors, etc. With increasing focus of the government towards financial inclusion, rising financial awareness, and increasing smartphone and internet penetration, there is a significant potential for expanding the reach of NBFC-MFIs.

We have presence in 27 states and union territories. To adapt to and mitigate risks while tapping into underpenetrated markets, we implement comprehensive risk management strategies. These strategies include developing robust credit scoring models using alternative data sources, leveraging advanced technologies for predictive analytics and fraud detection, and diversifying our portfolio across regions and sectors. Establishing strong governance and compliance practices, along with regular audits, ensures operational stability and adherence to regulations. We invest in staff training and educate our clients on responsible borrowing to further reduce default risks.

Responsible lending and customer- centric service delivery are fundamental to the sustainability of the microfinance business. Failure to adequately assess borrower capacity, prevent over-indebtedness, ensure fair treatment, or effectively address customer grievances may result in portfolio deterioration, regulatory action, reputational damage, and loss of customer trust. Conversely, robust customer protection practices, transparent communication, ethical lending, financial literacy initiatives, and superior customer experience strengthen customer relationships, improve repayment behaviour, enhance loyalty, and support sustainable business growth.

The Company follows robust credit underwriting standards, customer due diligence processes, borrower awareness programmes, portfolio monitoring mechanisms, and fair practices aligned with regulatory requirements. It has also implemented customer protection measures through adherence to the Client Protection Principles, Guardrails 2.0, and the Sparsh grievance redressal mechanism. Leveraging its phyGital model and digital innovations, the Company strives to deliver seamless, transparent, and customer-centric financial services while ensuring responsible lending practices and timely resolution of customer concerns.

Positive: Improved portfolio quality, customer retention, stronger customer loyalty, and sustainable business growth. Negative: Credit losses, regulatory scrutiny, reputational damage, and reduced customer confidence arising from inadequate lending or customer service practices.

Strong governance practices and ethical business conduct are essential for maintaining stakeholder trust, regulatory compliance, and long- term value creation. Governance failures, unethical conduct, fraud or non-compliance with applicable laws and regulations could expose the Company to legal, financial, and reputational risks. Conversely, robust governance frameworks enhance transparency, accountability, investor confidence, and access to capital.

The Company has established governance structures, Board oversight mechanisms, Codes of Conduct, whistleblower frameworks, compliance monitoring systems, and periodic internal audits to strengthen ethical business practices and regulatory compliance. Further, the Company’s governance framework is supported by active Board oversight and specialized committees led by Independent Board Members, ensuring effective supervision, accountability, and informed decision- making across the organization.
Positive: Enhanced stakeholder confidence and sustainable growth. Negative: Regulatory penalties, reputational damage, and loss of investor confidence in case of governance failures.

As a microfinance institution, the Company primarily provides unsecured loans to underserved and economically weaker section of the society. The absence of collateral increases exposure to credit risk, additionally borrower repayment capacity may be impacted by economic challenges, over-indebtedness, adverse climatic conditions, or other external disruptions. Managing borrower indebtedness continues to require close attention across the microfinance sector, particularly where customers have relationships with multiple lenders. Effective management of unsecured lending risk is therefore critical to maintaining portfolio quality, financial stability, and sustainable growth.

The Company has intensified scrutiny of borrowers with exposure to multiple lenders and regularly monitors portfolio quality through data- driven analytics. In addition, a risk- based internal audit mechanism, led by an in-house Internal Audit function, provides extensive oversight of critical and high- risk business areas, enabling timely identification and mitigation of emerging credit risks.

Negative: Increased delinquencies, credit losses, provisioning requirements, deterioration in asset quality, reduced profitability, and potential impact on liquidity, investor confidence, and long-term business growth.

As one of India's leading NBFC-MFIs, Satin Creditcare Network Limited plays a pivotal role in advancing financial inclusion by extending credit access to underserved and unbanked populations, particularly women entrepreneurs in rural and semi-urban areas. Despite significant progress in financial inclusion, a substantial section of the population continues to face barriers in accessing formal financial services due to limited credit history, geographical constraints, and socio-economic challenges. The growing focus of the Government of India on financial inclusion, women's economic empowerment, digital financial services, and entrepreneurship, presents a significant opportunity for the Company to expand its outreach while contributing to inclusive economic development. By providing responsible and accessible financial solutions, the Company supports income generation, livelihood enhancement, and financial resilience among low-income households.

Positive: Business growth, portfolio expansion, enhanced social impact, stronger stakeholder confidence, and access to sustainability- focused investors. According to the NCAER–MFIN study, regulated small-borrowing has played a transformative role in expanding financial inclusion, with dependence on informal borrowing declining from 46% of borrowers in 2011 to nearly 1% of borrowers accessing formal credit today.

The Company's growth and operational stability depends on continued access to diversified and cost-effective funding sources. Adverse market conditions, tightening liquidity, interest rate fluctuations, or disruptions in capital markets could impact funding availability and increase borrowing costs. At the same time, maintaining a diversified lender base and prudent risk management framework strengthens financial resilience and supports sustainable growth.

The Company maintains a diversified funding profile comprising domestic and international lenders, banks, financial institutions, and impact investors. SCNL’s funding strategy emphasizes diversification and balance across funding instruments, lender categories, and sources of capital, thereby enhancing funding resilience and reducing concentration risk. Robust asset-liability management practices, liquidity monitoring, stress testing exercises, and enterprise risk management processes further support the effective management of liquidity risks and ensure long-term financial stability.
Positive: Stable financial performance and investor confidence. Negative: Increased funding costs and financial losses during adverse market conditions.

Climate change poses direct and indirect risks to the Company's operations and customers. Extreme weather events, changing rainfall patterns, and climate-related disruptions can adversely impact the livelihoods and repayment capacity of borrowers, particularly those engaged in agriculture and micro-enterprises. Simultaneously, climate-conscious financing and environmentally responsible operations present opportunities to strengthen resilience, improve resource efficiency, and attract sustainability-focused investors and stakeholders.

The Company integrates climate considerations into business operations, promotes digital processes, monitors environmental performance, calculates its carbon emissions and explores sustainable finance opportunities
Positive: Enhanced resilience, improved reputation, and operational efficiencies. Negative: Increased credit and operational risks arising from climate-related disruptions.

1 Does the entity extend any life insurance or any compensatory package in the event of death of (A) Employees (Y/N) (B) Workers (Y/N)? (A) Employees - Y (B) Workers - Y Yes. The Company extends life insurance and EDLI benefits in the event of death of its employees. The Company offers three distinct types of coverage to its employees: Group Term Life (GTL), Employee Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI), and Group Personal Accident Policy (GPAP). a. GTL: GTL coverage varies according to the employee’s grade within the organization, ranging from INR 10 Lakhs to INR 1 Crores. This tailored approach ensures that employees and their families receive adequate financial support in the unfortunate event of the employee’s demise. b. EDLI: EDLI provides a fixed coverage of INR 7 Lakhs, serving as an additional layer of financial security for the employee’s family, irrespective of any other life insurance coverage the employee may hold. c. GPAP: GPAP offers a flat coverage of INR 10 Lakhs, extending financial assistance in the event of an accident leading to death or disability. Additionally, the Company provides the Satin Sahyog policy, aimed at providing support to the families of employees who have lost their lives while on duty. Eligible dependents, including spouses, children under 21 years, and parents without other means of support, benefit from this policy. The scheme entails a monthly payout of INR 10,000 to the nominee or guardian for minor nominees, offer term life insurance, including pension, education assistance and a job for family member and Mediclaim cover for the entire family, as applicable. Furthermore, the Compassionate Education Assistance Scheme under Satin Sahyog facilitates the education of dependent children under 18 years, with a maximum of two children per deceased employee. Each eligible child receives INR 2,500 per month in their guardian’s account until they reach the age of 18 years, or complete their 12th grade, whichever comes earlier.
